title: Augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW): a doubly robust effect
summary: A risk difference that is consistent if either the propensity model or the outcome model is right, with an influence-function standard error.

sizing._note: Sized as a two-group risk comparison; the unadjusted form is conservative when the working models are prognostic.

pinned_defaults: Both: logistic propensity and outcome models; mu1 = mean(m1 + A (Y - m1) / e), mu0 = mean(m0 + (1 - A)(Y - m0) / (1 - e)); unstabilized, untrimmed.
Both: SE = sd of the influence function / sqrt(n), ignoring the estimation of the two models; valid when both are right, and to be checked by bootstrap otherwise.
Written out in both languages; R's AIPW and tmle packages add cross-fitting and flexible models around the same estimator.
_double_robustness: Over 100 seeds, with the propensity model reduced to an intercept, AIPW's bias is -0.002 and weighting alone +0.125; with the outcome model reduced to treatment only, AIPW's bias is -0.002 and g-computation alone +0.125. harness/causal_examples.test.py asserts both.
